supersedes.reason: The first remediation closed the original attacks, but focused re-review found bare relative separator forms, Python mutable-base bypasses, and a TypeScript __proto__ snapshot-copy bypass. This record preserves both prior manifests and binds the second focused remediation.

checks.result: Deterministic generation, strict TypeScript typecheck, and all 20 contract tests across three files pass. Bare relative separators reject, known DOI/HTTP/Handle controls accept, and serialized __proto__ remains an own unknown key that rejects without prototype injection.

checks.command: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest tests.contracts.test_domain_contracts tests.foundation.test_adr_check tests.foundation.test_build_manifest tests.foundation.test_quality_check tests.foundation.test_ui_change_gate
checks.result: All 55 focused contract/foundation tests pass. Draft and generated Python reject both relative separator forms in observed/normalized fields; the immutable Mapping/tuple snapshot rejects ordinary assignment plus dict.__setitem__ and list.append base-method attacks.
All 16 focused Core API tests pass with the new truthful read-only Python decoder return type and canonical snapshot serializer.
Formatting, Ruff lint, and mypy pass for all 83 governed Python files. Report SHA-256: 66d2d9d2ea73427f656186ebca993bdb9232306b1647ce34c3608824c76b16b6.
ADR-0013 covers all 34 protected base-to-remediation paths and architecture passes. The domain-contract guide now states the scheme-aware separator and immutable Python serialization boundaries.
Clean deterministic build identity 0.1.0+g300a1a4 passes; build-manifest SHA-256 is c0980ee70208627184d9592cb3ff2fbd4c489f8bc5838c751597c7cee00c1205. Planning and generated views validate.

evidence: External identifiers are now selected through a scheme-aware union: separator-free portable text for ordinary schemes, recognized DOI/arXiv/Handle forms for scholarly separators, and HTTP(S) for URL identifiers. Bare forward- or backslash-relative path strings reject in both fields and runtimes.

Python decoders now return a truthful read-only Mapping/tuple graph rather than mutable subclasses, with canonical serialization through core_aggregate_snapshot_json; mutable base-class descriptors cannot apply.
TypeScript copies records into null-prototype containers, preserving every own JSON key through validation and preventing __proto__ assignment from changing the decoded prototype.

Cross-runtime/Draft tests cover private/paper.pdf and private\paper.pdf in observed and normalized fields, valid DOI/HTTP/Handle controls, dict.__setitem__, list.append, and an own serialized __proto__ object.
All original path/control/integer/caller-alias attacks remain covered and passing.

The second remediation changes only the portable schema/generator/generated artifacts, focused regressions, and truthful architecture documentation. Persistence, lifecycle, UI, dependencies, migrations, and T02/T03 ownership are unchanged.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: The remaining defects were isolated to separator classification and runtime snapshot representation. Focused schema/decoder, generated type, service import, quality, ADR, architecture, and build-inventory checks cover their credible impact.
verificationSelection.deferred: Full foundation/service profiles and cross-task lifecycle, restart, migration, and end-to-end qualification remain deferred to CAP-03.S01 slice review.

reviewerDisposition.note: Re-review only the three second-review findings, exact 11-file 787e501..300a1a4 range, supersession chain, and focused checks. Do not run broad profiles.
